term: per se nota, natural-law first principles
definition: In q.94 a.2, a proposition is self-evident in itself when its predicate belongs to the account of its subject; whether it is self-evident to us also depends on knowing its terms. Aquinas places the natural-law precepts alongside the first principles of demonstration and grounds the first practical precept in the notion of good. This source reading is not a corpus self_evident status and does not by itself close a frontier premise.
